correctness.rationale: Independently differentiating the Newton interpolant through 0,−a,−a−b,−a−b−c and substituting nodal differences yields precisely the published P/D and −U/D entries with unit shift below. At four successive chronological phases the product has trace T/Δ and determinant E/Δ; the positive one-step determinants also justify conjugacy under phase shift. The quadratic Schur test reduces to Δ−T+E, Δ+T+E, and Δ−E strictly positive. An independent integer polynomial-ring product matches every TSV entry, all of degree twenty, with counts 271,267,271 and minimum coefficients 6,6,3. This proves strict positivity on the full positive orthant, not a sampled set. In the full nodal state the constant coordinate is triangularly coupled to the damped difference block, so 1 is simple and geometric decay of differences gives convergence. The separate exact substitution h_i=r^i gives trace −1+6r−74r²/3+O(r³) and determinant r⁵/3+O(r⁶); the simple branch near −1 has modulus 1−6r+O(r²) and dominates the branch tending to 0. This proves sharpness of the supremum without weakening the pointwise strict inequality.
residual_risks: All assertions are for each fixed repeated positive pattern and y′=0. A strict Floquet damping margin uniform over quadruples is false; no general-grid estimate is established.

evidence: Li–Liao Thm. 3.1 uses adjacent-ratio bound R₃≈2.553 in a perturbed/general-grid result. The smooth-grid proof of Söderlind–Fekete–Faragó places ratios near unity. The cited older stability sources could not all be directly read.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The periodic ratios of (1,r,r²,r³) include r⁻³, so arbitrarily extreme fixed patterns lie outside either available hypothesis. Larger method or equation scope under bounded ratios is not dominance on the grid domain.

originality.rationale: The closest indexed all-ratio theorem is for three-periodic BDF3, not for four independent spacings. Its exact product and its boundary family are different. Relevant available BDF3 literature uses ratio or smoothness conditions not satisfied by the four-step geometric reset. The supported distinction is this exact fixed four-period positive family and its sharp reset branch, not the general Floquet method or Schur signs as a technique.

Existing three-periodic BDF3 record and ratio-restricted literature
value.rationale: Four-periodic grids are a natural next full Floquet family after two and three, not a single chosen ratio. The proof gives unrestricted stability across that entire family despite arbitrarily large adjacent ratios, and the exact reset limit identifies why fixed-grid damping cannot have a common strict spectral margin. The full-degree certificate tests a genuine gap not closed by an existing short-period stability test.
residual_risks: No larger-period, nonlinear, or forced stability classification follows.
